questions: Have you recently had any trauma or injury to your head or face?
Have you had any recent surgery, especially around your nose or eyes?
Are you experiencing any pain in or around your eye?
Is there any change in your vision?
Do you have any discharge from your eye?
orders: Urgent non-contrast CT of the head
Complete neurological examination including pupillary responses and fundoscopy
CT angiography of head and neck if CT shows hemorrhage or mass effect
served: deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses
results: 1. Urgent non-contrast CT of the head
CT head (non-contrast): multiple skull fractures and epidural haemorrhage; NO evidence of brainstem injury
2. Complete neurological examination including pupillary responses and fundoscopy
cranial nerve examination: limited right eye adduction failing to cross midline, with left abducting nystagmus on left gaze; otherwise normal
mental status / cognitive screen: impaired during acute traumatic encephalopathy
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
pupil size and light reaction: equal and reactive
4. CT angiography of head and neck if CT shows hemorrhage or mass effect
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Traumatic right internuclear ophthalmoplegia due to right medial longitudinal fasciculus injury from head trauma (associated with skull fractures and epidural haemorrhage)

Demyelinating disease (e.g., multiple sclerosis) with coincidental presentation after trauma

Focal brainstem contusion affecting the right MLF region

Vascular injury to perforating branches supplying the right MLF
